entries.answer: PHP is a server-side scripting language that was built in 1995 for generating web pages, and it has grown well past that origin into the language behind a large share of the web. It is interpreted, so a file is read and executed on request rather than compiled ahead of time, it is loosely typed with optional type declarations, and the language is procedural, object-oriented and functional all at once. The extension system is the reason PHP survived every prediction of its death: adding a feature is a C module loaded through an extension interface, which is how support for databases, images, encryption and dozens of other domains arrived without changing the core. The current major version is 8, which brought a large performance improvement, named arguments, match expressions and stricter typing, and a lot of advice online about PHP still describes a version that is two generations old.

entries.answer: Laravel is a full-stack PHP framework that provides the structure a web application needs so you are not assembling it from unrelated packages. Its parts are an ORM called Eloquent for database work, a Blade templating engine for views, a router, a queue system, a scheduler, authentication scaffolding and an Artisan command line tool that generates code, runs migrations and clears caches. The architectural idea is convention over configuration: the framework expects a file layout and class names in a particular shape, and it then finds everything without a list of mappings, which removes a category of configuration errors at the cost of a learning curve. It follows a model-view-controller structure, so requests go to a controller, the controller talks to a model, and the result is rendered through a view. A Laravel application is also a Composer project, so the dependency file is the thing you read to know what is installed.

entries.answer: Composer is the dependency manager for PHP and the counterpart to npm in the JavaScript world, and it exists because a PHP project of any size needs libraries it did not write. A composer.json file declares the packages the project needs and the PHP version they require, and running composer install reads that file, resolves the dependency graph, downloads everything into a vendor directory and writes a composer.lock file pinning exact versions. The lock file is the part that makes builds reproducible, and committing it is the recommended practice for applications, while a library deliberately does not commit it so its consumers can resolve their own. Composer also handles autoloading, generating the class map that lets your code reference a class without a pile of require statements at the top, and it can run scripts defined in the same file for deployment steps.

patterns: what is an associative array in php
how to add key value in php array
entries.answer: An associative array in PHP is the array type used for almost everything, including things other languages treat as objects and dictionaries, and it is the single most distinctive thing about writing PHP. It is written as key => value pairs inside square brackets, a string or integer key can address any element, and arrays here are ordered maps rather than the flat list that the name suggests elsewhere. Because it serves as a list, a dictionary and a structure at the same time, code like foreach and array_map works uniformly, and JSON decoding produces exactly this type. The sharp edge is comparison: a loose equality check asks whether two arrays have the same key and value pairs in the same order and with the same types, so arrays that look identical can compare unequal, which is why strict comparison is the safer habit. It also explains why a list in PHP can have a gap in its numeric keys, a valid and occasionally useful state that other languages do not have.
